cover.headline_html: 3 myths that stop great GovCon candidates.

myths.label: The Experience Trap
myths.myth_text: You need years of federal experience before you can compete for government contracts.
myths.reality_text: GSA Schedule only requires 2 years in business and demonstrated commercial revenue. Your federal track record starts the day your Schedule is approved.

myths.label: The Passive Discovery Lie
myths.myth_text: Once you have a GSA Schedule, government buyers will find and contact you automatically.
myths.reality_text: The Schedule is a contract vehicle, not a lead generator. You still need to market, respond to RFQs, and build relationships with contracting officers.

myths.label: The One-Time SAM Mistake
myths.myth_text: SAM.gov is a one-and-done registration — you sign up once and you're set.
myths.reality_text: SAM.gov requires annual renewal. A lapsed registration freezes your ability to receive federal payments — even mid-contract, even with an active award.

close.close_question: Drop the myth you believed when you first started looking at federal contracting.
